pageSubtitle: Explore the places, communities, and stories that have shaped San Francisco's Chinatown.
allPeriodsText: Choose a period above to highlight the sites connected to it and read about the broader history of that era. Sites are linked to a period by documented events or cultural significance — not only by when the current building was built.

about.heading: A developing student resource
paragraphs: *Chinatown Through the Ages* is a draft informational resource created by students in UC Berkeley's EDUC 155AC, in collaboration with the Chinese Historical Society of America (CHSA).

This is a work in progress. The selected sites, descriptions, and dates are preliminary and will be refined with community input. Every entry shows a verification label, and details that sources disagree on are marked {verify}. Please do not cite this prototype as an authoritative source.
Corrections and suggestions are welcome — especially from Chinatown residents, families, and organizations whose histories are represented here.

goals.title: Cultural preservation
goals.body: We focus on how places sustain traditions, language, faith, and community — not just on famous buildings.

goals.title: Change over time
goals.body: The timeline shows how Chinatown developed from the Gold Rush through exclusion, rebuilding, activism, and today.

goals.title: Why sites matter
goals.body: Each site explains its cultural significance and its role in supporting immigrants and preserving heritage.

goals.title: Accessible history
goals.body: An interactive map makes historical research approachable for visitors with no background in Chinatown's history.

goals.title: Community collaboration
goals.body: Content will be reviewed and refined with the Chinese Historical Society of America, whose guidance shapes which sites and stories are included.

footer.collaborationLine: In collaboration with the Chinese Historical Society of America
footer.sourcesText: Site-specific sources are listed in each location panel.
